section: Built for stores running Clover or PAX
text:
Built for stores running Clover or PAX
If your register is a Clover terminal or a PAX-based system, we connect directly to it. No new hardware, no changing how you ring up sales, no disrupting your day. We plug into what you already have.

title: Your POS system already knows what’s wrong with your business.
text:
What you’ll actually see








Margin, not just volume


Beer, wine, spirits, and tobacco carry very different margins. Volume lies; margin doesn’t — see which categories actually make you money.









Dead weight in inventory


Cash tied up in stock that isn’t moving, flagged automatically instead of hiding in plain sight on a shelf.









Vendor cost creep


Cost trends by distributor and SKU, tracked over time, so a quiet price increase gets caught before it eats your margin.









Stockouts on best sellers


Running out of a top performer is a lost sale you’d never otherwise see — flagged before it happens, not after.



See the full breakdown, with real numbers, on Why It Matters.

title: About
text:
I’m a Business Intelligence analyst working in renewable energy, where I build the ETL pipelines, automation, and dashboards that let a company actually see what its own data is telling it. I have a Bachelor’s from UCLA and a Master’s in Business Analytics from UCSD, and I’ve spent my career in Python, SQL, Power BI, and Power Query — the exact toolkit behind everything on this site.

UCLA UCSD, MS Business Analytics Python · SQL · Power BI Ocean Beach, San Diego

Independent liquor stores and smoke shops run on the same kind of POS data a Fortune 500 company pays a whole analytics team to interpret — margin by category, inventory turnover, vendor cost trends, seasonality. The difference is nobody’s built it for them. That’s the gap this consultancy exists to close: the same rigor, sized and priced for a business that’s never had it before.
I’m based in Ocean Beach, San Diego, and work directly with each store I take on — no account managers, no hand-offs, no generic templates pretending to be insight.

title: Services & Pricing
text: Every engagement starts the same way: we connect to your POS system, build out your dashboards, and get you comfortable with what you’re seeing. From there, pick the level of ongoing service that fits your store.

title: Services & Pricing
text:
One-time setup
A single setup fee covers connecting securely to your POS (Clover or PAX), building your canonical dashboard suite, and validating the numbers against what you already know about your business. Cost depends on your POS system and how much historical data we’re bringing in — you’ll get a fixed quote before anything starts, no surprises.

title: Services & Pricing
text:
Then, pick a monthly tier

Core Dashboard
Automated, always-current dashboards covering sales trends, margin by category, dead stock, and vendor cost tracking. Log in whenever you want the answer.
$99–149/mo


Core + Reporting
Everything in Core, plus a scheduled summary — daily, weekly, or monthly — sent straight to your email. No login required to stay on top of your numbers.
$199–249/mo


Insights + AI
Everything above, plus plain-English callouts on what changed and why (“beer margin dropped 4% this week, driven by a vendor price increase”), and automatic flags for unusual activity — sudden stockouts, discount patterns, voids worth a second look.
$299–399/mo


Predictive
Demand forecasting and reorder-point recommendations, once we’ve built up enough history on your store to make it reliable. Available as an add-on for established clients.
$399–599/mo

section: Why monthly, not a one-off project
text:
Why monthly, not a one-off project
A dashboard built once and never touched again goes stale within a season — your product mix changes, your vendors change, your seasonality shifts. Every tier here is a maintained, always-refreshed pipeline, not a static file. That’s what the monthly fee actually buys.
New clients: ask about founding-customer pricing — reduced setup and introductory rates in exchange for feedback while we build out support for your specific POS system.

title: Why It Matters
text:
Owners of independent liquor stores and smoke shops usually know their business by feel — which shelves move, which customers come back, which weeks are busy. That instinct is real. But it misses things that only show up in the numbers, and those blind spots are usually where the money is.
These are the questions our dashboards are built to answer first — see the specific tiers on Services & Pricing.

title: Why It Matters
text:
Margin, not volume
Your best-selling product by units is often not your most profitable one. Beer, wine, spirits, and tobacco carry very different margins — a fast-moving item can be quietly mediocre for your bottom line while a slower one is doing more work than you’d guess.

Seeing margin by category, side by side with volume, is usually the single most eye-opening thing an owner sees the first time.

title: Why It Matters
text:
Dead stock
Every dollar sitting in inventory that isn’t turning over is a dollar you can’t use elsewhere. Slow-moving stock hides in plain sight on a shelf — it doesn’t show up on a register tape, only in a report that’s actually looking for it.

title: Why It Matters
text:
Vendor cost creep
Most stores buy from more than one distributor, and prices move gradually enough that a small, steady increase rarely gets noticed until it’s already cost you real margin over a few months. Tracking vendor cost by SKU over time turns that into something you catch early, not something you discover in hindsight.

title: Why It Matters
text:
Stockouts on your best sellers
Running out of a top performer is a lost sale you never see on any report — unless something is actually tracking your stock levels against what normally sells. Flagging this before it happens (not after) is the difference between a missed Tuesday and a missed holiday weekend.

title: Why It Matters
text:
Seasonality
Liquor and smoke shop sales move hard around holidays, game days, and weather — patterns that are obvious in hindsight but easy to under- or over-order for in the moment. A year or more of history turns “I think it gets busy around then” into an actual plan.
